params.question: Is forward horizon the lever that raises the achievable IC information ratio, given that universe size is not?
params.background: docs/gate_feasibility_review.md decomposed per-date IC variance and found the binding constraint is signal instability, not measurement precision. True IC variation runs 0.38-0.40 while mean IC is 0.06-0.11, capping the ceiling near 0.27 at a 20-day horizon. Horizon is the only remaining candidate that could move the ceiling itself rather than the threshold.
params.hypothesis: Twenty-day forward returns are dominated by noise that momentum does not predict. At longer horizons the predictable component accumulates faster than the unpredictable one, so mean IC rises relative to its own time variation and the ceiling rises with it.

grid.layer: us_asset_rotation_reference — the decided strategy universe, held fixed. Layers are not swept.

params.primary_metric: ceiling = mean(IC) / sd(true IC), the information ratio implied when per-date sampling error is removed
params.overlap_correction: Monthly evaluation dates make forward windows overlap at every horizon above 20 days: 2 neighbours at 60 days, 5 at 120, 11 at 250. Overlap leaves each per-date IC unbiased but makes the series autocorrelated, so the naive se(IR) understates uncertainty and would make long horizons look more precise purely as an artifact. Standard errors use Newey-West with lag = ceil(horizon_days/21) - 1. A non-overlapping subsample — every k-th month-end where k = ceil(horizon_days/21) — is reported as a robustness check.

decision_rule.horizon_is_the_lever: Best ceiling across the grid reaches 0.35 or above AND the ceiling rises with horizon rather than spiking in one isolated cell. Then re-specify the gate horizon and register a follow-up.
decision_rule.horizon_is_not_the_lever: Best ceiling stays at or below 0.30. Then no remaining structural lever has been found and the 0.30 threshold must be re-derived from what this asset class can produce.
decision_rule.inconclusive: Best ceiling lands between 0.30 and 0.35, or improves only in a single non-monotone cell. Treated as not established, not as partial support.

params.why_0_35_and_not_0_30: Eight cells are measured and the decision reads the maximum, which is upward biased when each estimate is noisy. The 0.35 bar buys margin over both the 0.30 gate and the 0.273 already observed, so a win has to be larger than the selection bias it could be made of.
params.monotonicity_requirement: A real mechanism should show a trend across horizons. A single cell beating the bar while its neighbours do not is read as noise, not as a result, and this is committed before seeing any of it.
params.label_window_note: Forward returns for late in-sample dates extend past 2018-12-31 into cached 2019+ prices. That is label horizon, not lookahead into the strategy, and it is the same convention the existing 20-day report already uses.
params.not_in_scope: No threshold, factor, universe or strategy rule changes under this registration. It measures whether a lever exists.
